newsitem.title: USA: MedPartners says Coram reduces suit claim.
newsitem.headline: MedPartners says Coram reduces suit claim.

text.p: MedPartners Inc said Thursday that Coram Healthcare Corp had reduced its claim against MedPartners unit Caremark International Inc to $300 million from $5.2 billion.
MedPartners, whose subsidiary Caremark International Inc is the defendant in the lawsuit, said Coram announced the reduction during a pretrial conference at the Superior Court of San Francisco.
A spokeswoman for Coram declined to comment, saying the company was still evaluating the validity of the statement made by MedPartners.
Coram is suing Caremark for alleged fraud and breach of contract in connection with the sale of Caremark's home infusion business to Coram in 1995.
Meanwhile, MedPartners said Caremark had brought its countersuit against Coram to the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals in Chicago.
"The case has been remanded to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois for further proceedings," it said.
Caremark's $300 million securities fraud claim against Coram alleges false advertising, breach of confidentiality, among other things.
Its decision to bring its countersuit to Chicago reverses an earlier one in which it dropped 12 of the 13 causes of action in the San Francisco court.
MedPartners acquired Caremark International in a merger completed in September 1996.
Based in Birmingham, Alabama, MedPartners is a physician practice management company.
Coram from Denver, Colorado, provides health care services.
